title: Meta review: audit of the synthetic_reference review records and the findings they assert
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Meta review of the synthetic_reference review records authored in this pass: re-derivation of every finding they assert against the artifact content, plus a record-integrity audit of the record files themselves.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Provenance repair by a separate session (opencode-2026-10-01-provenance-repair), not a re-review. All 18 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (synthetic_reference).  18 of 18 named artefacts have been revised or had their bytes replaced since this review was issued, so this record is re-issued at revision 2 and its digest for those artefacts now names the current revision; per-artefact detail, including the superseded digest and the basis for each classification, is in digest_corrections.  The findings, dispositions, scope, checklist and reviewer_identity of the original pass are untouched by this repair. The digest refresh does not carry the weight of a re-review: the original reviewer session did not examine the current revision of the revised artefacts, and no substantive re-examination was performed here.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated.

scope: SCOPE IS PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY SO. This record audits the six synthetic_reference review records authored in this pass: FB2-REV-000003 (cybersecurity), FB2-REV-000004 (change management), FB2-REV-000005 (safety analyses and case), FB2-REV-000007 (verification planning) and FB2-REV-000009 (challenge pass). Because review.schema.json cannot reference a review artifact id (see FB2-REV-000184), those record files are audited through the artifacts they cover. reviewed_ids below is the COMPLETE UNION of the artifacts those five records covered: 33 artifacts, each enumerated with its digest. The union is listed so the accounting is exact, not to claim additional coverage: every one of these artifacts was already reviewed by the record named, and none is newly covered by this record. This record must not be read as a universal review of the synthetic_reference profile. The synthetic records FB2-REV-000008 (scope, planning and scenarios) and the as_is records are NOT audited here.

findings.description: Re-derivation of the findings asserted by the five in-scope review records: all 11 findings they carry were re-checked against the artifact content and all 11 hold as written. Specifically confirmed in this pass: the safety case timing arithmetic (FB2-REV-FND-000131), the safety case empty provenance (132), the dangling nested anchor SRC-HW-000001 (133), the duplicated independent-monitor statement (134), the as_is oracle-derivation gap (141, this profile's counterpart is FB2-REV-FND-000144), the tautological planning-stub expected outcomes (144), the constant-digest evidence defect (143), the absent security verification evidence (110), and the clean results for the change records (120, 121). No finding asserted by those records was found to be overstated, mislocated or unsupported. Recorded as a performed check.
findings.evidence: Each of the 11 findings was re-derived against the cited artifact field: the timing arithmetic re-summed from the FSR statements; SRC-HW-000001 re-confirmed absent from the 102-entry source registry; the 18 constant digest uses recounted across 6 execution records; the two evidence directories re-enumerated as empty; the 5 boolean-only planning-stub expected_outcomes re-read.

findings.description: Record-integrity audit of the five in-scope review record files: all of them pass schema validation, all carry production_authorized false, product_verification_credit false and human_approval_status pending, and all declare themselves as automated review output in lifecycle_status_note. No review record asserts human approval, tool qualification, certification, or an ASPICE capability level. However the audit also confirms the limitation already recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000184: because a review record cannot legally list another review record, none of these five record files appears in this record's reviewed_ids, and their own digests are therefore not bound by any reviewed_ids entry anywhere in the corpus. The record files' current sha256 values are recorded in the meta_audit.record_digests field of this record instead, which is weaker: a value recorded inside another record is not the same guarantee as a digest in a reviewed_ids entry, because nothing re-checks it.
findings.evidence: corpus.py validate reports 0 errors with these records present, so all five pass schema validation. A pattern scan across all five found no certification, tool-qualification, human-approval or ASPICE-capability claim. The digest of each record file is recorded in this record's meta_audit field; none of them appears in any reviewed_ids array because the schema forbids it.

dispositions.action: No action required on the findings themselves; all 11 re-derive. Recorded as a verified result so that the pass's own claims are attributable to a check.

Partially accepted. The policy-field and disclaimer audit is clean and needs no action. The digest-binding limitation is accepted and is the same framework gap as FB2-REV-FND-000184; recording record digests inside another record is an acknowledged stopgap, not a fix. No schema was edited and no check was weakened.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every artifact covered by this review. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit.

SCOPE: PARTIAL. Five of the eleven review records authored in this pass are audited. The synthetic records FB2-REV-000008 and FB2-REV-000012 itself, and the four as_is records, are outside this audit.

Self-audit by the same session is inherently weak. This record was authored by the same automated session as every record it audits, so 'all 11 findings re-derive' means one automated pass confirmed its own work, not that an independent reviewer agreed. Master-prompt section 15 assigns confirmation of repair to another pass; that has not happened.

No finding asserted by any in-scope review was weakened, downgraded to make a gate pass, or resolved by relabelling an artifact. No corpus.py check was edited. No artifact outside docs/artifacts was touched.

Verification performed: (a) all 11 findings of the five in-scope records re-derived from cited artifact fields; (b) corpus.py validate re-run with all records present, 0 errors; (c) pattern scan of the five record files for certification, tool-qualification, human-approval and ASPICE-capability claims; (d) sha256 of each record file recomputed. All four performed; (a), (b) and (c) clean.
review_method: Independent re-derivation of each asserted finding from the cited artifact field, corpus validation re-run, prohibited-claim pattern scan over the record files, and recomputation of each record file's content digest.

meta_audit.record_digest_binding_blocker: review.schema.json artifact_id pattern admits only three-segment ids; review ids have two segments
